title: Long multiplication
goal: I can multiply a 3- or 4-digit number by a 2-digit number.
teach: Split the 2-digit number into tens and units. Multiply by the units, then by the tens (start that row with 0 in the units place), then add the two rows. The area model shows why it works: 46 × 23 = 46 × 20 + 46 × 3.
tvis: 800 + 120 + 120 + 18 = 1 058, so 46 × 23 = 1 058.
watch:
In the second row you multiply by tens, so write 0 in the units column first.

Problem-solving lens
Estimate first: 346 × 27 ≈ 350 × 30 = 10 500. An answer of 9 342 is close, so it is sensible.
